texts.preamble: Sri.Niranjan K.M. S/O K.N.Manohar vs Aged About 45 Years on 4 October, 2021 In The Court Of The Lxiii Addl.City Civil & Sessions Judge (Cch-64) At Bengaluru. Dated this Monday the 04th day of October 2021 P R E S E N T :- Sri. B.Venkatesha B.Sc., Ll.B., Lxiii Addl.City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City. Crl.A. No.1559/2016 Appellant/ Sri.Niranjan K.M. S/o K.N.Manohar Respondent : Aged about 45 years, Residing at No.365, 8th Main, Milk colony, Malleshwaram West, Bengaluru - 560 055. (By Sri.Maniklal M. Dhangadi, Adv.,absent.
texts.facts: The appellant has filed this appeal U/Sec.29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondent challenging the order dated 28-09- 2016 passed in Cr.Misc.51/2011 on the file of Court of M.M.T.C-IV, Bengaluru. Appellant is the R.1 and respondent is the petitioner before the trial court. Therefore, for the sake of convenience, the parties to this 2 Crl.A.1559/2016 appeal are herein afterwards referred with their ranks before the trial Court. 2. The brief facts as set out in the memorandum of appeal are that before the trial Court, the petitioner has filed petition under Secs.12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the R.1 to 4 seeking reliefs under Secs.19, 20 and 22 of the Act contending that she is the legally wedded wife of R.1 in view of solemnization of her marriage with him on 08-11-2000 at Dwarakanath Bhawan. Out of the said wedlock, one female child was born. The petitioner has alleged that R.1 to 4 have demanded her to pay gold and silver articles. Therefore, after her marriage, R.1 has started to harass her for dowry. He abused her for silly reasons in a filthy Sri.Niranjan K.M. S/O K.N.Manohar vs Aged About 45 Years on 4 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35916104/ 1 language. He deprived her of food, cloth and affection by inflicting physical and mental cruelty on her. Therefore, she has filed a complaint against R.1 to 4 before the Subramanyanagara Police Station. Police have enquired the residents and has warned them not to cause domestic violence on her. But, the respondents have continued their acts of causing domestic violence on her. She has contended that the respondents owned a house. The 1 st respondent is having a wholesale business of medicine. He has sufficient source of income. In spite of it, the respondents have neglected and refused to provide basic needs to her and her child. Therefore, she is in need of Rs.50,000/- p.m as maintenance. She has sought for grant 3 Crl.A.1559/2016 of Rs.2 lakhs as compensation towards the domestic violence caused by the respondents on her. Therefore, she has sought for grant of the reliefs as prayed against R.1 to 4 before the trial Court. 3. On service of notice of the said petition, R.1 to 4 have put their appearance before the trial Court through their Advocate and have filed their common written objections contending that the petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12(1) of PWDV Act is not maintainable either in law or on facts. They have admitted that marriage of the petitioner was solemnized with R.1 on 08-11-2000 at Dwaraka Bhavan, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru. R.1 is residing in a rented house along with his parents and brothers and running a small medical store. R.1 to 4 have denied all other specific allegations that made against them as false. They have contended that R.1 has received one gold ring weighing 5 grams, one bracelet weighing 12 grams, chain weighing 8 grams, one colour TV, one fridge, TV Stand only from the parents of the petitioner. He has not received any cash nor demanded the petitioner to give cash and other gold items as alleged. The R.1 to 4 have specifically denied that they demanded the petitioner to pay dowry amount, gold and silver articles as alleged. They also have specifically denied that they subjected the petitioner to a domestic violence as alleged in the petition. Thereafter, R.1 has made a separate house and that she returned on 01-11-2012 and stayed with him up to 23- 11-2011 and went back to her parents house. During that time, she lived with him happily. The R.1 had only Bank balance of Rs.3,705/- as on 26-07-2000. The petitioner is getting a monthly rental income of more than Rs.40 to 50 thousand. The 1st respondent's mother is undergoing medical treatment. R.1 himself spending money towards her medical treatment. At the time of marriage, R.1 gave 100 grams of gold jewelry including other silver items and 5 costly silk sarees with 20 grams of Mangalasuthra to the petitioner. The respondents have pleaded that the petitioner has filed the petition just to harass them. A dispute is pending before the Family Court at Bengaluru. The petitioner has collected a sum of Rs.4 lakhs as on the date of complaint saying that she will deposit it in the name of her daughter. But, she has not mentioned anything about receipt of the said money. The respondents have further pleaded that just to take advantage of the fact, though MC petition is pending before the Family Court, the petitioner has filed this petition though she is having sufficient income. The respondents are having very meager income. Therefore, the respondents are all have sought for dismissal of the petition filed by the petitioner. 5 Crl.A.1559/2016 Sri.Niranjan K.M. S/O K.N.Manohar vs Aged About 45 Years on 4 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35916104/ 2 4. Before the trial Court, the petitioner herself got examined as PW.1 and examined one Ramugopal as PW.2. She got exhibited 20 documents as Ex's.P.1 to 20 and closed her side of evidence to substantiate her claim. R.1 only examined as RW.1 and has got exhibited 5 documents as Ex's.R.1 to 5 and closed his side of evidence to substantiate defence of R.1 to 4. 5. On considering the petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of PWDV Act, the objections of R.1 to 4, evidence of PW's.1 and 2, RW.1, contents of Ex's.P.1 to 20 and Ex's.R.1 to 5 and upon considering the arguments urged before it, the trial Court has partly allowed the petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of the DV Act. The trial Court has dismissed the petition of the petitioner that filed in respect of passing of residence order etc. Along with the appeal, the R.1 has filed IA under Sec.5 of Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 62 days in filing this appeal contending that his mother is suffering from bone cancer and that therefore he is unable to contact his Advocate. The petitioner has not filed any objections to the IA filed under Sec.5 of Limitation Act. After filing of this appeal, R.1 and his counsel are remained as absent.
texts.arguments: The respondents have contended that after the marriage, the petitioner had stayed with R.1 only up to February-2001 4 Crl.A.1559/2016 thereafter she had left the company of R.1 and has gone to her parents house voluntarily for the reason best known to her. Being aggrieved by the impugned order of the trial Court, R.1 has filed this appeal contending that the impugned order of the trial Court is bad in law and the materials placed on record. Therefore, this court has appointed Sri. Zabiulla standing counsel and advocate as amicus curie to assist this court for disposal of this appeal Heard the arguments of both sides on merits of this Sri.Niranjan K.M. S/O K.N.Manohar vs Aged About 45 Years on 4 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35916104/ 3 appeal. 4 As per Sec.2(a) of PWDV Act, 2005 aggrieved person means any women who is, or has been in domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic vigilance by the respondent. As per Sec.2(f) of PWDV Act, 2005 Domestic relationship means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of the 1 Crl.A.1559/2016 marriage, adoption or are family member living together as joint family. As per Sec.2(e) of PWDV Act, 2005 Domestic incident report means a report made in the prescribed form on receipt of a complaint of domestic violence from an aggrieved person. As per Sec.2(s) of PWDV Act, 2005 shared household means a household where the person aggrieved lives or any stage has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent and includes such a household whether owned or tenanted either jointly by the aggrieved person and the respondent, or owned or tenanted by either of them in respect of which either the aggrieved person or the respondent or both jointly or singly have any right, title, interest and equity and includes such a household hold which may belong to the joint family of which the respondent is a member, irrespective of whether the respondent or the aggrieved person has any right, title or interest in the share household. Sec.3 of PWDV Act, 2005 defines the meaning of Domestic Violence, which provides as under; 3. Definition of domestic violence.--For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it-- (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse, 11 Crl.A.1559/2016 sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse; or (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b); or (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person. Explanation I.--For the purposes of this section, Sri.Niranjan K.M. S/O K.N.Manohar vs Aged About 45 Years on 4 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35916104/ 5 (i) "physical abuse" means any act or conduct which is of such a nature as to cause bodily pain, harm, or danger to life, limb, or health or impair the health or development of the aggrieved person and includes assault, criminal intimidation and criminal force; (ii) "sexual abuse" includes any conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates the dignity of woman; (iii) "verbal and emotional abuse" includes-- (a) insults, ridicule, humiliation, name calling and insults or ridicule specially with regard to not having a child or a male child; and (b) repeated threats to cause physical pain to any person in whom the aggrieved person is interested. (iv) "economic abuse" includes-- (a) deprivation of all or any economic or financial resources to which the aggrieved person is entitled under any law or custom whether payable under an order of a court or otherwise or which the aggrieved person requires out of necessity including, but not limited to, household necessities for the aggrieved person and her children, if any, stridhan, property, jointly or separately owned by the aggrieved person, 1 Crl.A.1559/2016 payment of rental related to the shared household and maintenance; (b) disposal of household effects, any alienation of assets whether movable or immovable, valuables, shares, securities, bonds and the like or other property in which the aggrieved person has an interest or is entitled to use by virtue of the domestic relationship or which may be reasonably required by the aggrieved person or her children or her stridhan or any other property jointly or separately held by the aggrieved person; and (c) prohibition or restriction to continued access to resources or facilities which the aggrieved person is entitled to use or enjoy by virtue of the domestic relationship including access to the shared household. Explanation II.--For the purpose of determining whether any act, omission, commission or conduct of the respondent constitutes "domestic violence" under this section, the overall facts and circumstances of the case shall be taken into consideration. The petitioner is also entitled to Rs.10,000/- per month towards her and her child's maintenance. The petitioner has not filed any appeal against the finding of the trial Court that she fails to prove that the R.1 to 4 have subjected her to a domestic violence and have neglected her. But, the R.1 has contended that though the trial Court has held that the petitioner fails to prove the fact of domestic violence, but the trial Court has erred in granting maintenance and compensation amount. PW.2 Ramagopal, the cousin brother of the petitioner also has deposed his side of evidence by supporting the evidence of PW.1 and the facts as averred in the petition. Sec.23(2) of the Act provides that if the Magistrate is satisfied that an application prima facie disclosed that the respondent is committing an act of Domestic Violence, he may grant an order on the basis of affidavit etc. Sec.23(1) provides that Magistrate may pass such interim order as a deems just and proper. Sec.22 of the Act provides that the Magistrate may pass order directing the respondent to pay compensation and damages for the injuries including mental torture and emotional distress caused by the facts of domestic violence committed by that respondent.
